html:
The Battle of Gaixia was fought in the winter of 203 to 202 BCE at Gaixia, in today's Anhui province in eastern China. Liu Bang, king of Han, destroyed the army of his rival Xiang Yu of Chu and became the first emperor of the Han dynasty.

The Qin dynasty had collapsed in 206 BCE, and the rebel leaders fought over what was left. Xiang Yu won most of the battles, but Liu Bang was better at keeping allies and supplies. After four years they agreed to divide China, but Liu Bang broke the truce and chased Xiang Yu east. Several armies, the largest under the general Han Xin, closed in on the hungry Chu army at Gaixia. The story goes that the Han soldiers sang songs of Chu at night, so that Xiang Yu's men thought their homeland had fallen, and many deserted. Xiang Yu broke out with a few hundred riders and killed himself at the Wu River.

Liu Bang took the title of emperor within months. The Han dynasty lasted about four centuries and gave its name to the Chinese people. The story is told by Sima Qian and is still played in Chinese opera.
